quarterly_data.signal: Record Q2: order intake at a new all-time high of just above SEK 22 billion — total growth 35.2%, of which 28.5% organic and 8.6% from structure (mainly BU Cryogenics) — with solid demand across almost all of the business, Service included (Service organic growth 10%). Sales SEK 18.1 billion (+7.7%, 5.9% organic); operating income SEK 2.9 billion; adjusted EBITDA margin 17% (in line with group target); EPS SEK 4.91. Book-to-bill 1.23. Large orders overall at a normal level — not the main growth driver. Another step in the SEK 100 billion growth plan for 2030.
quarterly_data.figure: Order intake just above SEK 22 billion (+35.2%, 28.5% organic); sales SEK 18.1 billion (+7.7%); book-to-bill 1.23; operating income SEK 2.9 billion; EBITDA margin 17%; EPS SEK 4.91

quarterly_data.signal: Record order book of SEK 53.5 billion — SEK 29.1 billion currently planned for 2026 delivery and SEK 24.5 billion already booked for 2027 — supporting continued invoicing growth, assessed in line with current input cost levels. Energy Division orders grew 70% ('even a bit above our own expectations'), all parts of the division growing WITH DATA CENTERS LEADING THE WAY; Cryo contributed about SEK 1.5 billion of orders including a breakthrough US large-scale LNG cold-box order. Q3 order intake expected somewhat lower sequentially than the record Q2 — historically that wording indicates ending above SEK 20 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: Record order book SEK 53.5 billion (SEK 29.1 billion for 2026, SEK 24.5 billion for 2027); Energy Division orders +70%; Cryo orders ~SEK 1.5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Data centers: the 12-month order pace in data centers in the Energy Division is approximately SEK 5 billion (below SEK 2 billion booked in the quarter itself; run-rate guided at SEK 2-2.5 billion recent quarters). 'We are very confident that our market share has increased during this year' — Alfa Laval describes itself as the GO-TO PARTNER AND ANCHOR PARTNER for most data-center expansion plans on the thermal side, deliberately MANAGING how far into 2027/2028 it books orders (order intake is a managed number; think run-rate). Growth beyond thermal: data-center demand creeping into the flow/valves side (hygienic white-room fluid handling) — an opportunity of about SEK 1 billion in complementary products long term; no M&A planned to expand DC exposure.
quarterly_data.figure: Data-center 12-month order pace ~SEK 5 billion; ~SEK 1 billion long-term opportunity in complementary flow products

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity is the constraint on converting record orders: most load factors are 'really high' — to a level that becomes less productive (air shipments to manage lead times); Energy Division margin dented by slight negative mix, provisions/reserves, inflation, currency and uneven load in some units (Welded, Cryo — Cryo quickly resolved by the Q2 order book). Data-center demands to scale are high: current CapEx levels kept in the MEDIUM TERM to support customer agreements PAST 2027 — full-year CapEx SEK 2.5 billion-SEK 3 billion, expected to remain at that level a couple of years; capacity increases coming online in this year and importantly beginning of 2027 are already essentially fully booked, and NEW capacity investment decisions are being made now against underlying 2028+ demand. US fluid-handling capacity from investments a year/year-and-a-half ago now coming online.
quarterly_data.figure: FY CapEx SEK 2.5 billion-SEK 3 billion, staying elevated a couple of years; 2027 capacity additions essentially fully booked

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook: business conditions expected to remain positive short-to-medium term; underlying market activity confirmed to be somewhat higher than previously anticipated. Q3 2026 order intake expected somewhat lower sequentially vs the record Q2 (Marine about the same level; Energy and Food & Pharma lower). Q3 guidance: CapEx up to SEK 1 billion, amortizations SEK 170 million, tax 24%-26%. Full year: CapEx SEK 2.5 billion-SEK 3 billion, amortizations SEK 680 million. Expects to be cash flow positive for the year; heat pump business trending toward SEK 2 billion annualized in a competitive market.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 orders somewhat lower sequentially (historically implies above SEK 20 billion); FY CapEx SEK 2.5 billion-SEK 3 billion
